title: Video Calls and Meetings
short: Join on time, check your sound and background, mute when not speaking, look at the camera, and give the meeting your attention.
trouble: Learners multitask with the camera off and get caught when asked a question. Treat a video meeting like a room you walked into.

blocks.html: You learned the basics of video calls and of phones in company. A video meeting for work or school joins the two: it is a room you walk into, even if it is on a screen.
Join on time, check your sound and background, mute when you are not speaking, look at the camera, and give the meeting your attention.

Everyone in a video meeting has blocked out the same minutes. Joining late or fumbling with sound wastes everyone's time at once. Background noise from an open microphone drowns out whoever is speaking, which is why muting matters. Looking at the camera is how you make eye contact on a screen, and keeping your attention on the meeting is the same courtesy you would show in a room.

opts.title: Joining a video meeting
items: Test your camera and microphone a few minutes early
Choose a quiet spot with light on your face
Join on time, and say hello
Mute when you are not speaking
Unmute, look at the camera and speak when it's your turn

blocks.title: A barking dog
blocks.q: In the middle of a team call, Priya's dog starts barking. What should she do?
steps: She mutes right away so the noise doesn't cover the speaker.
If she needs to speak, she says, "Sorry, one moment," settles the dog, and comes back.
No long apology is needed; these things happen.
blocks.a: Mute at once, and keep it light.

blocks.title: Caught multitasking
blocks.q: Leo turns his camera off and answers emails during a meeting. The manager asks him a question. What went wrong, and what is better?
steps: He wasn't paying attention, so he can't answer.
Better: keep the camera on when the group does, close other windows, and take notes on the meeting.
blocks.a: Give the meeting full attention, as if in a room.
